question: Determine the domain and range of $f(x)=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{x-1}{x+1}\right)$. Explain why one value lying inside the principal range of $\tan^{-1}x$ is excluded from the range of $f$.
explanation:
Restriction from the denominator
The rational expression is defined when $x+1\neq0$. Hence, the domain is $$\mathbb{R}-\{-1\}.$$

Range of the rational expression
Let $$t=\frac{x-1}{x+1}.$$ Solving for $x$, we obtain $t(x+1)=x-1$, so $$x=\frac{-(1+t)}{t-1}.$$ This expression provides a real value of $x$ for every real $t$ except $t=1$. Therefore, the range of the inner expression is $\mathbb{R}-\{1\}$.

Application of inverse tangent
The function $\tan^{-1}t$ maps $\mathbb{R}$ onto $\left(-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$. Since $t=1$ is excluded, the corresponding value $$\tan^{-1}1=\frac{\pi}{4}$$ is also excluded.

Final result
The range is $$\left(-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right)-\left\{\frac{\pi}{4}\right\}.$$

options.A: Domain: $\mathbb{R}-\{1\}$; Range: $\left(-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right)-\left\{-\frac{\pi}{4}\right\}$; the excluded value corresponds to the unattainable inner value $-1$
options.B: Domain: $\mathbb{R}-\{-1\}$; Range: $\left[-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right]$; no value is excluded because the inner expression can take every real value
options.C: Domain: $\mathbb{R}$; Range: $\left(-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right)-\left\{\frac{\pi}{4}\right\}$; the excluded value corresponds to the unattainable inner value $1$
options.D: Domain: $\mathbb{R}-\{-1\}$; Range: $\left(-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right)-\left\{\frac{\pi}{4}\right\}$; the excluded value corresponds to the unattainable inner value $1$
